name: Chokebore
label: AmRep
lede: Two brothers, a Honolulu skate scene, a demo that landed in Minneapolis, and a sadcore band that ended up sleeping in vans across Europe more than it ever did at home.

eras.title: From Dana Lynn to Chokebore
eras.text: Three friends from Honolulu's skate and punk scene, one brother off to art school in Los Angeles, and a lot of time as a trio before the band had a name that stuck.

years.h: Honolulu punk kids start a band as Dana Lynn
years.p: [[Troy von Balthazar|66003585-5be1-4afa-8d37-e7c43743232b]], Jon Kroll and James Kroll meet in Hawaii's punk and skating scenes, and start out under the name Dana Lynn.
years.xp:
Troy told Flipside in 2000 that the three met around 1990 and played in several Honolulu bands, one called Mug. Dana Lynn only became Chokebore when the band was getting ready to put out records on Amphetamine Reptile.

Troy also said he was not originally the singer. He learned to sing along the way, and had changed his birth name Bruno to Troy at sixteen to escape teasing.

years.h: Jon Kroll moves to LA for art school; the others follow
years.p: Jon goes to Los Angeles for graduate study in art, and the rest of the band plays on as a three-piece for about 18 months, including six months in San Francisco.

eras.title: The demo that reached Minneapolis
eras.text: A demo lands on Tom Hazelmyer's desk, and within months Chokebore has a picture-disc 7-inch, a debut album and a slot on Nirvana's last American shows.

years.cap: Chokebore in their first AmRep year
years.h: A demo tape reaches Amphetamine Reptile Records
years.p: In March 1993 the band's demo arrives at the Minneapolis label run by [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]], and AmRep signs them on the strength of it.
years.xp:
By the band's own account, the trio had reunited with Jon Kroll in the winter of 1992 before the tape went north. AmRep followed up with the picture-disc 7-inch Nobody / Throats to Hit in May 1993.

Chokebore's dynamics, quiet then sudden, sounded unlike much of the AmRep catalog. The band wound up filed under sadcore anyway.

years.h: Motionless · AmRep 020, recorded in Minneapolis
years.p: The debut was recorded at AmRep's own Minneapolis studio with engineer Tim McLaughlin, with a cover designed by Hazelmyer.
years.xp: Johnee Kop plays drums. The album includes Hit Me, a reworking of Rod Stewart's Do Ya Think I'm Sexy? that keeps only the original verses. Coat got a video by David H. Moe on an AmRep video compilation.

years.h: Clusterfuck tour with Today Is The Day and Guzzard
years.p: Three AmRep bands share a bill for a fall 1993 US tour, after Chokebore had already gone coast to coast with Australia's Cosmic Psychos.

years.h: Ten shows opening for [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]
years.p: Chokebore joins [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] and the Butthole Surfers for ten shows on the west coast, some of the last American dates of [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]]'s band.
years.xp:
Chokebore's own biography describes a ten-show support run with Nirvana and the Butthole Surfers. Wikipedia describes them among the openers on Nirvana's last ten American shows. Exact dates vary by source.

A French interview also lists Deftones and Tool among the bands Chokebore later opened for.

years.h: Clusterfuck goes to Europe: one bus, three bands, 30 shows
years.p: The same AmRep package crosses 11 countries in one bus, and Europe starts to become Chokebore's real home audience.
years.xp: Troy said in 2000 the band spent seven to eight months a year touring Europe. Wikipedia says the band did better commercially there than at home, especially after Anything Near Water.

eras.title: Bitter, pretty and loud
eras.text: Two records that made the case for Chokebore, a drummer swap, and a long run of European touring.

years.h: Anything Near Water · recorded at Motiv in Los Angeles
years.p: Producer Biff Sanders records the second album in LA, the last one with original drummer Johnee Kop.
years.xp: Sanders engineered and co-produced with the band. A 7-inch, Thin as Clouds, followed the same year. Vicious Circle reissued the album on orange vinyl in 2013 for the band's 20th anniversary.

years.h: Christian Omar Madrigal Izzo takes the drum stool
years.p: Christian Omar Madrigal Izzo starts touring with Chokebore in 1995 as Johnee Kop leaves.

years.h: A Taste for Bitters · recorded in a French village
years.p: The band tracks its third album in spring 1996 at Black Box studio in Noyant-la-Gravoyère, France, with engineer Peter Deimel, while touring Europe.
years.xp: Released on October 2, 1996 on AmRep, it was the first record with Izzo on drums. Marcos Siega directed a video for the title track. The band also shared a split 7-inch that year with German band Tocotronic.

years.h: Darren Doane directs the video for It Could Ruin Your Day
years.p: The band puts out a single, It Could Ruin Your Day, and Darren Doane films its video.

eras.title: Leaving AmRep, staying on the road
eras.text: The band moves to European label Boomba, turns over drummers again, and toils through brutal touring before a long quiet.

years.h: Black Black is recorded back in France
years.p: Chokebore records its fourth album in February 1998 at Black Box, this time with new drummer Mike Featherson, and releases it April 13, 1998 through Boomba in Europe.
years.xp:
The US release came September 10, 1999 on Punk in My Vitamins. The band has said the title came from a Japanese chewing gum brand. The CD version adds a 15-minute closing track, The Rest of Your Evening.

Chokebore's site calls it the band's high point.

years.h: Featherson out, Izzo back
years.p: Mike Featherson leaves after the Black Black cycle, and Christian Omar Madrigal Izzo returns to the kit after about two and a half years away.

q: Troy von Balthazar, on being asked if he was always the singer
years.h: Eighty shows straight and the van takes its toll
years.p: In a 2000 Flipside interview Troy describes playing eighty shows straight, and the mental strain of life in a van.
years.xp: He also talked about playing odd rooms, including Sarajevo and the Arctic Circle, since Europe was where Chokebore had its crowd.

years.h: Strange Lines EP comes out on Redwood
years.p: Chokebore returns to release after a long stretch of touring and silence with the EP Strange Lines.

years.h: It's a Miracle on Pale Blue
years.p: After four years of work and silence, Chokebore puts out its fifth album, a looser, more personal record.
years.xp: Pale Blue also reissued Motionless and Anything Near Water that year, with new artwork by Jonathan Kroll. The band's site calls the album more mature and less sad than what came before.

eras.title: Break, solo records and a return
eras.text: The band goes on hiatus in 2005, everyone scatters into other projects, and then a European reunion turns into a new EP.

years.src: Wikipedia · exitmusik.fr · Troy von Balthazar Wikipedia
years.h: Chokebore goes on indefinite hiatus
years.p: Troy von Balthazar later said some members had children and other commitments and that being great means giving everything.
years.xp: Troy started making solo records: home-recorded EPs from 2001 as B. Balthazar, then a deal with French label Olympic Disk and a 2005 debut recorded at Elliott Smith's old studio. Izzo toured with Christian Death 1334, and Jon Kroll began the wordless guitar project A Newborn Riot Of Dreams.

years.h: Chokebore announces a reunion
years.p: On November 18, 2009 the band posts on its homepage that it is getting back together for a handful of European shows.

years.src: Vicious Circle Bandcamp · Concert and Co
years.h: Falls Best EP on Vicious Circle
years.p: A five-track EP released October 10, 2011 is the band's first new studio release in nearly a decade.
years.xp: Vicious Circle opens with Lawsuit and closes with Awesome. The band toured Europe behind it, including a Paris show at La Machine du Moulin Rouge on October 31, 2011.

years.h: Vicious Circle reissues the AmRep albums for the 20th anniversary
years.p: Motionless comes out on white vinyl and Anything Near Water on orange.

eras.title: Back in print
eras.text: Two labels put the old records on vinyl again.

years.h: Black Black returns on vinyl
years.p: Vicious Circle reissues Black Black in December 2024, and Amphetamine Reptile follows with its own vinyl in May 2025.
